title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 121
paragraphs: It is a matter of wonder to me, and I do not accept the report, that the Alcmaeonidae could ever have flashed a shield to the Persians by pre-arrangement, with the wish that the Athenians should fall under the barbarians and under Hippias. They are plainly shown to have been haters of tyrants as much as, or more than, Callias son of Phaenippus, the father of Hipponicus — Callias, who was the only Athenian who dared, when Pisistratus was driven out of Athens, to buy up the goods that were being auctioned off by the state, and who in other ways also devised every kind of hostility against him.
